mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.25% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 50% of instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts over three consecutive months signals a strengthening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where HOUST increased for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production by more than 1% in a month indicates a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market participants react to the weakening economic conditions.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where INDPRO decreased by more than 1% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% in the same period, it signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where both PAYEMS and UNRATE met the trigger conditions.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% month-over-month and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) remains stable (change < 0.1%), it indicates real demand growth without inflationary pressures, which is conducive to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 1% and CPIAUCSL change < 0.1% in 1 month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of instances where both RSAFS and CPIAUCSL met the trigger conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a loosening monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as financial conditions ease.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS decreased for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3% in the same quarter, it signals robust economic growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases > 2% and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 quarter
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of instances where both GDPC1 and UNRATE met the trigger conditions.
